# Patch against succinctlabs/flock 83f963e8ede6d9a85ec4762b0c018943b6f6542b

Nine changes; `Cargo.toml` inlines the workspace-inherited fields and points the sibling Flock
crates at the pinned git revision. Everything else is a verbatim copy of `crates/flock-core`
at that revision (`src/`, `configs/`).

## 1. Prover-only: the merged opening's weight vector (`src/pcs/jagged.rs`)

Only `build_merged_weight_and_prime` (the merged opening's weight vector `W`) is changed.

Why: Flock bakes, for every ring-switched claim, a 16 x 256-entry fold table (64 KB,
4,096 fold evaluations) per used word column of the committed stack, whatever the column's
height. A one-row table type with `2^16` word columns (the bridge instance of
`agg-keccak`, `docs/keccak.md`) then spends 3.4 s and 6.4 GiB in this step for a
stack of `2^16` words, and a full segment would need 51 GiB. The patch evaluates such
claims per slot instead, `φ(eq_col[c]·r)` with one multiply and one fold-table lookup,
whenever the stack averages fewer than `BAKE_MIN_HEIGHT = 64` live rows per used column
(`ColSide::Short`). Flock's own shapes (hundreds of rows per column) keep the bake.

Prover-only and exact: `x ↦ φ(eq_col[c]·x)` is F₂-linear, so the baked byte decomposition
and the direct evaluation compute the same `W` bit for bit; the proof bytes, the transcript
and the verifier are unchanged, and proofs made with this copy verify with upstream Flock.

Addition (agg-mldsa): a ring-switched claim's column whose factor `eq_col[c]` is zero
contributes the zero map, so it is neither baked (`bake` returns early) nor swept (the
segment sweep skips it, writing zeros if the claim is the first). The bit claim of the
parity chain addresses 64 of the sponge's 2,156 used word columns. Exact for the same
reason; `W` is unchanged.

## 2. A Ligerito parameter set: `LigeritoProfile::Slim8`

`src/pcs/ligerito.rs` and `src/pcs/commit.rs`: a sixth profile, `Slim8`, with `Slim`'s
accounting (analysis `f256_split_johnson_two_point_ood_query128_c3_algebraic_row_union_over_bchks25_thm_4_6`,
16-bit query PoW, the +2/level ladder, the same `initial_k` rule, the strict 128-bit
grinding policies of the non-Ligerito challenge families) at level-0 rate 1/8
(`log_inv_rate` 3, so the ladder runs 3, 5, 7, ...). Every `match` on the profile gains the
variant in `Slim`'s arm; nothing else changes, so the five shipped profiles derive, validate,
prove and verify exactly as upstream. Its configs `configs/ligerito/m{22..35}_slim8.toml` are
generated by Flock's own `LigeritoSecurityConfig::derive_profile(m, Slim8)` and checked by
`validate()` (`crates/agg-keccak/examples/gen_slim8_configs.rs`, which also asserts that the
same derivation reproduces the shipped `m*_slim.toml` byte for byte). Level-0 queries 79
(Slim 119, Fast 244), level 1 48 (Slim 60).

This is a verifier-visible addition (a new parameter set of an unchanged protocol): proofs
under `Slim8` verify with this copy only, or with upstream Flock given the same configs.

To regenerate (Sections 1 and 2; Sections 3 to 9 below have their own lists, including the
level-1 `blocked.rs` encoder): copy `crates/flock-core/{src,configs}` of the revision above here, write the
`Cargo.toml` of this directory, re-apply the `ColSide::Short` hunk (three edits in
`build_merged_weight_and_prime`: the enum variant and the `bake_columns` decision, the
`Folded` claim arm, and the segment sweep arm), re-apply the `Slim8` arms, create empty
`m{22..35}_slim8.toml` files and run the example to fill them.

## 3. Prover-only: x86 SIMD kernels chosen at run time

Upstream selects its x86 kernels with `cfg(target_feature = ...)`: they run only in a
build with `-C target-cpu=native` (Flock's own `.cargo/config.toml`). Our default build
must not rely on SIMD, and a global `x86-64-v4` build breaks Akita, so the CLMUL timing
build ran Flock's portable kernels in its hottest loops. This copy checks the CPU once at
run time (`src/simd.rs`: `is_x86_feature_detected!`, cached in an atomic) and calls the same
`#[target_feature(enable = ...)]` kernels when the CPU has them:

| Kernel | Features | Call sites |
| --- | --- | --- |
| additive NTT butterflies (`butterfly_row_pair`, `butterfly_fused_2layer`, `butterfly_fused_4layer_row`) and the fused-4 schedule choice (`fused4_ok`, two places in `ntt/additive_ntt_f128.rs`) | `avx512f`, `vpclmulqdq` | `ntt/additive_ntt_f128/kernels.rs` |
| zerocheck round 1: `shift_reduce_inner_ab` (GFNI AVX-512, else GFNI SSE), `bit_transpose_64bytes` (`avx512vbmi`), `accumulate_convert_with_s_hat_v` (VPCLMULQDQ) | as listed | `zerocheck/univariate_skip_optimized/kernels.rs` |
| inverse-NTT table `apply` (`ell = 64`) | `avx512f` | `ntt/inv_table.rs` |
| zerocheck round 2 (`fold_pair_run`; the upstream inline block moved verbatim into `fold_pair_run_x86_avx512`) and the fused fold + message (`fold_and_message_x86_avx512`, given its `#[target_feature]`) | `avx512f`, `vpclmulqdq`, `sse4.1` | `zerocheck/multilinear.rs` |
| zerocheck round 2 message-only (`fold_pair_run_x86_avx512::<_, false>`), without output stores or scratch buffers | `avx512f`, `vpclmulqdq`, `sse4.1` | `zerocheck/multilinear.rs` |
| Ligerito induced basis (`scaled_xor_into_avx512`), with scalar fallback and zeroed allocation | `avx512f`, `vpclmulqdq` | `pcs/ligerito.rs` |
| zerocheck packed round 3 (`round3_task_avx512`), with wide products reduced once per equality block | `avx512f`, `vpclmulqdq`, `sse4.1` | `zerocheck/multilinear.rs` |

The AVX-512 GF(2^128) helpers those kernels use (`ghash_mul_x4`, `f128x4_loadu`,
`f128x4_set`, `WideGhashX4`) are copied from `flock-field` 83f963e
(`gf2_128/x86_64.rs`) into `simd::x86` without their `cfg(target_feature)` gates;
`flock-field` itself is unchanged and stays the pinned git dependency. Kernel bodies are
upstream's; the dispatchers add bounds asserts the upstream callers relied on implicitly
(the fused shift-reduce reads 8 bytes per K-row offset; the fold + message kernel needs
`a_in = 2 a_out = 4 eq_lo` and an even `eq_lo` length).

Exact and prover-only: every kernel computes the same GF(2^8)/GF(2^128) values as the
portable code, so commitments, transcripts and proof bytes are identical whichever path
runs (tests below; mode-A aggregates at 256 and 1,024 records are byte-identical to the
unpatched build under `FLOCK_SIMD=portable`, `gfni` and the full set). `FLOCK_SIMD` in
the environment caps the level for A/B runs: `portable` (or `off`) disables every x86
kernel, `gfni` keeps only the SSE GFNI one. On a CPU without the features (or another
architecture) the portable code runs as before.

### 3.1 Pair-aligned round 3 and packed-row bounds

The AVX-512 round-3 fast path moves four packed rows at a time and takes the both-pairs-live
shortcut only when `y + 4 <= end` (not `y + 2 < end`, which put only the first of the two
positions inside the interval). Its layouts are built with `LiveLayout::new_pair_aligned`,
which asserts even interval bounds; the generic `LiveLayout::new` still serves the interval
rank tests. The sparse round-2 entry points also assert that the live-pair list fits both
packed inputs (`16` bytes per pair) before the first raw read.

Tests (every path available on the CPU against the portable one; `simd::with_mask` limits
the features for one closure): `ntt::additive_ntt_f128::kernels::tests::x86_kernels_match_portable`,
`ntt::additive_ntt_f128::tests::every_kernel_path_matches_scalar` (whole transforms incl. the
fused-4 schedule and `from_message`), `zerocheck::univariate_skip_optimized::kernels::tests::*`,
the upstream x86 oracle tests made runtime-gated (`x86_gfni_sse_inner_matches_scalar_inner`,
`x86_gfni_avx512_inner_matches_scalar_inner`, `apply_x86_matches_apply_scalar`,
`fold_round2_pair_x86_matches_scalar`), and `zerocheck::tests::every_kernel_path_gives_the_same_proof`
(a whole zerocheck proof at m = 13, 16, 18 under every mask). Run them with
`cargo test --release --manifest-path vendor/flock-core/Cargo.toml --lib` (the crate is
outside the workspace; use a separate `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, with and without
`RUSTFLAGS="-C target-feature=+pclmulqdq"`).

To regenerate: re-apply the call-site edits listed in the table (each replaces a
`cfg(target_feature)` pair by `if simd::has(...) { unsafe { kernel(...) }; return; }`
before the portable call), drop the `cfg(target_feature)` gates of the x86 kernel modules
and items (keep `cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")`), point their GHASH imports at `simd::x86`,
and copy `src/simd.rs`.

## 4. Prover-only: AVX-512 block statistics of the merged opening

`pcs.rs::block_first_phase` computes, per ring-switched claim, term `j` (128 of them)
and block `e`, `S_j[e] = frob(kappa * sum_b pw[b][kinv_j] * bank[e][b], j)`: one scalar
multiply per `(j, e, b)` and `j` scalar squarings, plus a dot product per column for the
scalar claim groups. At 8,192 records (516 terms x 2,048 blocks) this was about 1 s of
the sponge opening. `src/pcs/block_stats_x86.rs` computes the same values when
`simd::has(AVX512_CLMUL)`: the inner products four terms at a time with lane-wise
deferred reduction (`simd::x86::LaneAccX4`; reduction is F_2-linear, so the reduced
sum equals the sum of reduced products), `kappa` and the squarings with `ghash_mul_x4`
across four blocks (field-identical to the scalar multiply), the dot products with
`WideGhashX4`. At the AVX2 width `s_vectors_avx2` and `dot_avx2` run the same inner
products two terms at a time through `simd::ghash2::Wide` and keep the portable byte-table
Frobenius, which does one lookup per byte instead of `j` dependent squarings. The terms
are pushed in the portable order. Measured locally (CLMUL build, 3 threads, load 6-7):
block statistics 800-1,000 ms -> 77-95 ms at 8,192 records; at 4K with six Flock threads
the AVX2 tier went from 113 ms to 93 ms (portable to two-lane kernels). Aggregates are
unchanged. Tests: `pcs::block_stats_x86::tests::{kernels_match_portable,
avx2_kernels_match_portable}`.

## 5. Verifier-visible: list-aware work at the outer sites

`src/zerocheck.rs` (`ZerocheckGrinding`), `src/lincheck.rs` (`LincheckGrinding`),
`src/pcs.rs` (`OpeningGrinding`), `src/pcs/jagged.rs` (`MultipointGrinding`),
`src/pcs/ligerito.rs` (`LigeritoProfile::l0_list_factor`) and `src/pcs/commit.rs`
(`PcsParams::{zerocheck, lincheck, opening}_grinding`).

Why: the outer challenges of a Flock proof (zerocheck, lincheck, ring switch, transport claim
batch, merged and multipoint rounds) are drawn before Ligerito's level-0 two-point binding,
so the Flock paper (Appendix A "Security", Remark 11) charges each of them the level-0
Johnson-list size `L_max = 1 / (2 eta sqrt(rho_0))`. Upstream's `per_challenge_128`
schedules include it only at the transport claim batch (6 bits, assuming `log2 L < 6`), which
leaves the other sites at about 122 to 124 work-normalized bits and `Slim8`'s claim batch at
127.86 (agg-mldsa `docs/soundness.md`).

The change: each policy gains `per_challenge_128_listed(list)` with `list = ceil(L_max)`
(36, 50, 71 for `Fast`, `Slim`, `Slim8` at `eta = 0.02`; `l0_list_factor`) and grinds
`floor(log2(numerator * list)) + 1` bits at every outer site: zerocheck initial point
`bits(m list)`, skip point `bits(127 list)`, rounds `bits(2 list)`; lincheck `alpha` and each
`beta` `bits(list)`, rounds `bits(2 list)`, skip point `bits((2^k - 1) list)`; ring switch
`bits(7 list)`, claim batch `max(6, bits(list))`, merged rounds `bits(2 list)`; multipoint
rounds `bits(2 list)` and batch `bits((K - 1) list)`. `per_challenge_128()` is
`per_challenge_128_listed(1)`, i.e. upstream's schedule; `PcsParams` selects the listed
schedules for `Fast`, `Slim` and `Slim8` (`Secure`, unique decoding, and the `*100` profiles
are unchanged). The AG-basis skip points keep upstream's bits (not used by agg-mldsa). The
proof bytes do not change (nonces are 8-byte words); the transcript validity rule does, so
proofs made with this copy do not verify with upstream and vice versa. Together with
Section 6 this is the verifier-visible protocol change of the vendored copy; it should be
dropped if the Flock authors give an argument for the outer sites without the list factor.

To regenerate: re-apply the listed schedules of this section in the files named above.

## 6. Verifier-visible: canonical nonce width

`src/challenger.rs` (`POW_NONCE_SLACK_BITS`, `pow_nonce_is_canonical`, the extension trait
`CanonicalPow`) and every verifier call site of a proof-of-work check (39 sites in
`zerocheck.rs`, `zerocheck/ag_skip.rs`, `lincheck.rs`, `lincheck/union.rs`, `pcs.rs`,
`pcs/ring_switch.rs`, `pcs/jagged.rs`, `pcs/ligerito.rs`, `pcs/ligerito/extension.rs`,
`matrix_fold.rs`, `product_gkr.rs` and `element_r1cs/{zerocheck, lincheck, union}.rs`).

Why: upstream's verifier accepts any `u64` nonce that passes the predicate, so the nonce of a
`g`-bit site has no fixed width and a proof has many valid nonce variants. Akita and Aerie fix
the width at `g + 7` bits (Akita `GRINDING_NONCE_SLACK_BITS`, Aerie C.1) and their verifiers
reject anything else; our PIOP and tie nonces follow them (`docs/soundness.md`).

The change: the verifier calls `verify_pow_canonical`, `verify_pow_and_sample_f128_canonical`
and `verify_pow_and_sample_f128_vec_canonical`, which run the challenger's own check
(absorbing the nonce exactly as before, so the transcript is unchanged) and additionally
reject a nonce of `g + 7` or more bits (`g > 0`) or a nonzero nonce at a site without work.
The prover is unchanged: Flock's `grind_pow` returns the smallest passing nonce, which is at
least `2^(g + 7)` with probability `(1 - 2^-g)^(2^(g + 7)) <= e^-128 = 2^-184.66` per site; such
a proof is refused (a completeness event, counted in `docs/soundness.md`). Upstream's own
tests that search for a failing nonce with `verify_pow` (`pcs/ring_switch.rs`,
`pcs/jagged.rs`) and the `RoundGrindProver` forwarding impl (`zerocheck/ag_skip.rs`) keep the
plain check. Unit tests: `challenger::tests::{canonical_width_is_bits_plus_seven,
wide_passing_nonces_are_rejected}`.

To regenerate: copy the additions of `src/challenger.rs`, then in every other file replace
`.verify_pow(`, `.verify_pow_and_sample_f128(` and `.verify_pow_and_sample_f128_vec(` by their
`_canonical` forms outside the three places named above and add
`use crate::challenger::CanonicalPow;`.

## 7. Verifier-visible: a multilinear skip basis for ring-switched claims

`src/lincheck.rs` (`SkipPoint::Eq`, its arm in `SkipPoint::weights`, panic arms in
`sample_fresh`, `phi8` and the two lincheck skip-round matches), `src/lincheck/union.rs` (the
union lincheck's skip-round match) and a test in `src/pcs/ring_switch.rs`.

Why: agg-mldsa's tied part (tied-part proof version 5, `docs/parity-chain.md`) ends its parity
chain, a sum-check over the committed bits, with an evaluation of the sponge commitment's BIT
polynomial at a fully multilinear point. Flock's ring-switched claims carry a `SkipPoint` for
in-word bits 0..5, with the `phi_8` univariate-skip basis (`Phi8`) or the AG basis (`Ag`) only.
The verifier uses a ring-switched claim's skip point only through `SkipPoint::weights(6)`, the
64-entry functional that `ring_switch::build_claim_weights_from_skip` tensors with bit 6
(`pcs::verify_batch_merged`); the prover's ring switch never sees it (`s_hat_v` depends only on
the multilinear suffix).

The change: a third variant `SkipPoint::Eq([F128; 6])` whose functional is the eq tensor over
the six coordinates (index bit `k` on coordinate `k`), so a ring-switched claim at it is a plain
bit-MLE evaluation. The claim check `claim = sum_i w_i s_hat_v[i]` is exact for any linear
functional, and the reduction after it (`r''`, the packed claim) does not involve the basis, so
the ring-switch analysis is unchanged. A zerocheck or lincheck skip round never carries the new
variant; the paths that sample or grind a fresh skip point panic on it. Proofs that do not use
it are byte-identical to before. Test: `pcs::ring_switch::tests::claim_check_with_the_eq_skip_
basis_is_the_bit_mle` (the claim check with the eq weights equals the bit-MLE; the succinct
verifier accepts the honest ring switch and rejects another value).

To regenerate: add the variant and the arms named above.

## 8. Prover-only: scalar kernel engineering (CLMUL build, every CPU)

Pure evaluation-order and data-layout changes; every route computes the same field elements
(canonical residues, exact XOR sums), so proofs, transcripts and the verifier are unchanged and
aggregates are byte-identical to main.

- Diagnostics: `FLOCK_ZC_TIMING` reports the zerocheck tail per route (sparse, expansion, fused,
  naive; `FLOCK_ZC_ROUNDS` per round), `FLOCK_NTT_TRACE` the interleaved NTT's top/deep split,
  `PCS_TRACE` the block rounds' folds, `q'` and `W'` parts.
- Zerocheck round 1, portable path (`zerocheck/univariate_skip_optimized/kernels/portable.rs`,
  `ntt/inv_table.rs`): the shift-reduce kernel works on 64-lane bit planes (a 128 KiB bit-plane
  image of the inverse-NTT table, schoolbook GF(2^8) products on planes, one reduction and one
  plane-to-byte transpose per window; a log/exp kernel for other widths; the software-multiply
  kernel stays the test oracle), the C bit transpose uses delta swaps, and the per-lane window
  sums accumulate unreduced 256-bit products (`kernels::LaneAcc`).
- Additive NTT (`ntt/additive_ntt_f128.rs`): the four-layer top pass on x86 builds with
  `pclmulqdq` (`FLOCK_NTT_NO_FUSED4=1` restores fused-3 where no AVX-512 kernel runs; other
  targets keep fused-3), and the deep pass
  runs block-major once a block fits 512 KiB (`FLOCK_NTT_DEEP_BUDGET_LOG2`).
- Merged opening (`pcs.rs`, `pcs/block_stats_portable.rs`): portable block statistics mirror
  the AVX-512 structure (bank row read once, unreduced inner products, Frobenius powers from
  16 byte tables built once per process); the block rounds fuse fold and next message per term
  (parallel above 2^16 elements); `W'` tables are built in parallel.
- Lincheck (`lincheck.rs`, `lincheck/union.rs`): stripes with `k_log >= 14` fold with a
  column-partitioned kernel (`partial_fold_packed_z_rows_iblock`: shared subset-sum tables,
  register tiles, no per-task full-width accumulator or cross-task sum), at several row points
  per pass (`union_bitbank_fold_multi`); on x86 the single-table dispatch
  (`partial_fold_packed_z_best`) takes it for the same shapes.

- Lane-blocked level-0 codeword (`ntt/additive_ntt_f128/lane_blocked.rs`,
  `kernels::{blocked4_layer, blocked4_fused_2layer}`, `merkle::merkle_tree_lane_blocked`,
  `pcs::commit::{CodewordLayout, CodewordRows}`): `commit_lane_major` stores the codeword in
  groups of four lanes (`codeword[((l / 4) n + p) 4 + l % 4]`, lanes past the committed count
  zero). Pass 1 reads the message lanes once, skips the replicate layers, applies up to eight
  layers inside a 1 MiB tile and writes it with SSE2 streaming stores; pass 2 transforms
  cache-resident blocks through the remaining layers with the existing butterfly kernels. The
  Merkle leaves are the rows as before (gathered sixteen per batch); the Ligerito level-0 opens
  read rows through `CodewordRows`. The interleaved path stays as the fallback for shapes too
  small for the tiling; `FLOCK_LB_TILE_LOG`, `FLOCK_LB_TOP` tune pass 1.
- Blocked level-1 Ligerito encode (`ntt/additive_ntt_f128/blocked.rs`:
  `encode_blocked`, `blocked_deep_layers`, `stream_copy`; `pcs/ligerito.rs`: `ligero_commit`
  and `LigeroWitness::row`): at a level with sixteen lanes and at least `2^18` message
  columns, one call gathers the message rows and applies the first layers inside a block;
  the BLAKE3 leaves are hashed in the same pass and the transformed level is discarded, so
  the opening recomputes a queried row through `blocked_deep_layers`. Smaller levels keep
  the interleaved encoder. Same codeword, tree and opened rows.
- Level-0 leaves hashed in the encode (`AdditiveNttF128::encode_lane_blocked_hashed`,
  `merkle::GroupLeafHasher`, `CodewordLayout::LaneBlocked4Pending`,
  `CodewordRows::rows_at`): for BLAKE3 rows of at most 64 lanes, pass 1 takes ten layers and
  pass 2 runs over a position range of every group, absorbing each transformed group block
  into the range's leaves (a lane group is one BLAKE3 message block; sixteen leaves per
  AVX-512F call, a scalar compression otherwise). By default the final codeword is not
  stored: the buffer keeps the pass-1 state and the level-0 opening recomputes each queried
  row with only the butterflies that reach it. The `Keep` and `Off` arms remain as the test
  oracle (`lane_blocked_commit_matches_interleaved`). Same tree, cap and opened rows in all
  three.

- **Union lincheck fold and bit banks in one pass over `z`** (`lincheck/union.rs`,
  `lincheck/kernels/x86_64.rs`): `union_bitbank_fold_multi` reads the BatchMajor `z` once, builds
  the subset-sum tables of every row point per row tile and bit-transposes each run of eight
  rows in registers (no byte stripe is stored). `prove_union_with_z_vec_with_grinding` takes the
  lincheck's fold from it. Same vectors as the stripe fold, same proof bytes.

Tests: `zerocheck::univariate_skip_optimized::kernels::{portable::tests, tests}`,
`pcs::block_stats_portable::tests`, `pcs::block_round_tests`,
`lincheck::tests::partial_fold_iblock_matches_row_prefix_and_dense`, the NTT path tests (also
under `FLOCK_SIMD=portable` with a 4 KiB deep budget),
`ntt::additive_ntt_f128::lane_blocked::tests::matches_interleaved_transform`,
`pcs::commit::tests::lane_blocked_commit_matches_interleaved` (cap, whole tree and rows, each
`FusedMerkle` mode), `ntt::additive_ntt_f128::lane_blocked::tests::hashed_encode_matches_encode_and_leaves`,
`merkle::tests::group_leaf_hasher_matches_hash_leaf`.

The changed files this section describes also include `src/merkle.rs` (the grouped leaf
hasher and `merkle_tree_from_prehashed_level`), `src/ntt/additive_ntt_f128.rs` (the
`blocked` module) and `src/lincheck/kernels.rs` (the `bank_lookup_avx512` and
`bank_transpose_avx512` re-exports).

`AGG_ALLOC_POISON=1` also fills a buffer handed out from `take_f128`, `take_hashes` and
`take_u8` with `0xA5`. The pools' contents are unspecified, so a caller that reads a slot
before writing it otherwise silently consumes a previous prove's bytes; the poison mode makes
that visible to the byte gates.

The `FLOCK_INDUCE_CHUNK_LOG` knob selects the induced-basis chunk size; `0` selects the reference implementation. The default chunk log is 11. The SIMD kernel is selected once per chunk through the existing runtime feature dispatch.

## 9. Removed experiment switches

The default path is byte-for-byte unchanged in every case; the switch and its
non-default arm are gone.

- `FLOCK_HUGEPAGE` and `scratch::advise_hugepage`: opt-in
  `madvise(MADV_HUGEPAGE)` on Flock's codeword and tree allocations. It measured
  slightly slower than the `agg` binary's global allocator advice, which already
  covers large blocks.
- `FLOCK_NO_VIRTUAL_A` and `FLOCK_NO_VIRTUAL_B`: certification knobs that forced
  the materialized/round-0-JIT arms of the virtual eq basis. The shipped
  virtual basis stays; `VIRTUAL_A_OVERRIDE` still lets the byte oracle and bench
  alternate the lazy and materialized RS arms.
- `FLOCK_NO_STATS_LADDER`: forced the incremental L0 fold ladder instead of the
  block-statistics ladder. The block-statistics ladder stays.
- `FLOCK_NO_FOLD_LOOKAHEAD`: forced plain per-round folds instead of the
  alternating lookahead schedule. The alternating schedule stays.
- `FLOCK_NO_CLOSED_RS`: restored the pointwise message for aligned RS shapes.
  The closed-form message stays and the fallback body is removed.
- `FLOCK_NO_PREFAULT`: benchmark toggle that disabled hiding the codeword
  allocation behind witness generation. The single-threaded guard stays.
- `FLOCK_LIG_BLOCKED`, `FLOCK_LIG_FUSED_MERKLE`, `FLOCK_LIG_DISCARD`: Ligerito
  level-0 encode A/B switches. The blocked, fused and discard paths stay
  selected by shape and hash kind; the `FusedMerkle::Off`/`Keep` arms remain
  for the commit oracle.
- `FLOCK_LB_FUSED_MERKLE`: the same choice for the lane-blocked level-0 commit.
  `commit_lane_major` takes `FusedMerkle::Discard`; the enum arms stay for the
  test oracle.
- `FLOCK_COMMIT_INTERLEAVED`: forced the interleaved encoder. The lane-blocked
  encoder stays the shipped path; the interleaved path stays for shapes too
  small for the tiling.
- `FLOCK_TREE_PREFAULT`: A/B toggle for recycling the Merkle tree from the
  scratch pool. The pooled tree stays; the per-commit `vec!` arm is gone.
- `FLOCK_FOLD_RULE=sqrt`: capped √-rule fan-out for sub-gate folds, measured
  slower than serial (about 5.0 -> 4.6 ms at μ=20). Sub-gate folds stay serial.
- `FLOCK_ALLCORE`, `PCS_COMBINE_PCORES_ONLY`, `LINCHECK_PCORES_ONLY`: topology
  overrides for the all-core hops. The `ecore_rich_topology` gate is the only
  policy; the all-core pool still wins on 4P+4E and loses on 10P+4E.

Remaining diagnostics and A/B switches in the shipped tree (the defaults keep the shipped
path): `FLOCK_L0_LIVE_SKIP=0` restores the full `2^initial_k` level-0 ladder instead of
working on the live lanes; `FLOCK_LB_PASS2_COPY=1` copies a pass-2 block before the in-place
transform; `FLOCK_ZC_BITS_ROUNDS=0` disables the packed round-2/round-3 zerocheck path;
`FLOCK_ZC_SPARSE_SIMD=0` disables the AVX-512 sparse fold; `FLOCK_LB_TIMING_SHAPE=log_d,r,t`
and `FLOCK_BENCH_LOG_D` select the ignored timing tests' shapes.

### 3.2 The AVX2 tier and the `AGG_ISA` cap

`src/simd.rs` also parses `AGG_ISA=avx512ifma|avx512|avx2|scalar` once per process and uses
it as an upper bound on the feature bits. `scalar` clears every bit; `avx2` keeps the
AVX2 tier (x86-64-v3 plus PCLMULQDQ) and the optional 256-bit VPCLMULQDQ and GFNI
extensions, and clears every `avx512*` bit; `avx512` allows AVX-512 without IFMA; unset (or
`avx512ifma`) detects everything. `FLOCK_SIMD` still applies on top and can only lower the
result. `ghash_width()` chooses, in order, 512-bit VPCLMULQDQ, 256-bit VPCLMULQDQ,
128-bit PCLMULQDQ, or the portable kernels. `flock_core::simd_report()` states the cap and
the selected width.

The GF(2^128) primitive modules are `simd::ghash4` (512-bit, re-exports `simd::x86`),
`simd::ghash2` (256-bit VPCLMULQDQ) and `simd::ghash1` (128-bit PCLMULQDQ). Each exposes
the same functions (`loadu`, `storeu`, `splat`, `set_from`, `xor`, `mul`, `even_odd`,
`wide_zero`, `wide_acc`, `wide_fold`). The kernels below are generated once per family from
a macro and instantiated for all three widths, so every width computes the same field
elements:

| Kernel | Widths | Call site |
| --- | --- | --- |
| additive NTT butterflies and the fused-4 schedule decision (`x86_ntt_simd`) | 4, 2, 1 lanes | `ntt/additive_ntt_f128/kernels/x86_64.rs`, `kernels.rs` |
| zerocheck round 1 window accumulation | 4, 2, 1 lanes | `zerocheck/univariate_skip_optimized/kernels/x86_64.rs` |
| zerocheck round 2 fold (`fold_pair_run_x86_*`) and fold + message (`fold_and_message_x86_*`) | 4, 2, 1 lanes | `zerocheck/multilinear.rs`, `.../kernels/x86_64.rs` |
| zerocheck packed round 3 (`round3_task_*`) | 4, 2, 1 lanes | `zerocheck/multilinear.rs` |
| Ligerito induced basis (`scaled_xor_into_*`) | 4, 2, 1 lanes | `pcs/ligerito.rs` |
| lincheck bank lookup (`bank_lookup_avx2`) and subset-sum table build (`build_sum_table8_avx2`) | 2 lanes (AVX-512 keeps its 4-lane kernel) | `lincheck/union.rs`, `lincheck/kernels/x86_64.rs` |
| 64-byte bit transpose (`bit_transpose_64bytes_sse2`) | SSE2 (AVX2 tier) | `zerocheck/univariate_skip_optimized/kernels.rs` |
| BLAKE3 group leaf hasher (`blake3_groups::absorb8`) | 8 lanes (the AVX-512 kernel stays at 16) | `merkle.rs` |

The x8 hasher writes two eight-lane batches into the existing 16-wide state rows, so
`state_len` and `finish` are unchanged. The AVX-512 arm of every dispatcher is guarded by
the `avx512*` bits, which `AGG_ISA=avx2` clears, so no AVX-512 instruction of this crate
executes under that cap (`crates/agg-cli/tests/all/isa_cap.rs` checks the startup report).

Tests: `ntt::additive_ntt_f128::kernels::tests::{x86_128,x86_256,x86_512}_kernels_match_portable`
(odd lane counts and every block shape), `zerocheck::multilinear::tests::
avx2_round2_kernels_match_portable_with_odd_lengths`, `pcs::ligerito::tests::
scaled_xor_kernels_match_scalar_for_tails`, the mask-driven `merkle::tests::
group_leaf_hasher_matches_hash_leaf` and `lincheck::union::tests::
union_bitbank_fold_multi_matches_stripe_fold`, and the round-1 tests that iterate every
mask. The 1,024-record gate is byte-identical with `AGG_ISA` unset, `avx2` and `scalar`,
and with `AGG_ALLOC_POISON=1`.

To regenerate: keep section 3's edits, add the `ghash2`/`ghash1`/`ghash4` modules to
`src/simd.rs`, replace each AVX-512-only kernel body by a `macro_rules!` body instantiated
for the three widths, and replace the `has(AVX512_CLMUL)` call sites by the width
dispatchers (`*_best` helpers or `match ghash_width()`).

### 3.3 The AVX2 tier's remaining hot kernels

Three kernels were still paying for the narrower width at 4K, and each now has a dedicated
256-bit body:

* `pcs/jagged.rs::fold_and_round_oop_par` (the merged sumcheck's per-round fold and
  message) was scalar. Its AVX2 arm (`fold_and_round_avx2`) folds four outputs per pass
  with `ghash2`, accumulates both message products unreduced, and reduces once per
  chunk. It is about 1.3x faster than the scalar chunk on six threads, where memory
  traffic caps the gain; the scalar body remains for every other width.
* `lincheck/kernels/x86_64.rs::bank_lookup_avx2` reloaded each byte for the two
  point pairs of a four-point table line. `bank_lookup_pair_avx2` now shares the byte
  load and the table offset across both 256-bit halves; the 32K-shape single-thread
  bit-bank fold went from 45.7 ms to 35.7 ms (the AVX-512 kernel measures 28.1 ms).
* `simd::ghash2::wide_reduce` keeps the two lanes separate, which the block statistics
  above need.

`flock_core::f128_avx512_kernels()` exposes the selected GF(2^128) width to callers that
size a thread pool by it.

### 3.4 The round-1 inverse-NTT apply and bit transpose

Round 1 was the largest AVX2 loss at 32K, and most of it was not arithmetic width but call
overhead: `zerocheck/univariate_skip_optimized/kernels/x86_64.rs`'s AVX2 shift-reduce kernel
called the generic `InvNttTableByteSingleGf8::apply` eight times per input byte row, so
every call paid the runtime dispatch, the slice asserts and a 64-byte store followed by a
reload. Two targeted edits:

* `ntt/inv_table.rs::apply_x86_avx2_register_unchecked` is the AVX2 counterpart of the
  existing AVX-512 register-returning apply: it returns the 64 F_8 outputs in two
  `__m256i` and never leaves registers. The AVX2 shift-reduce kernel now calls it twice per
  `K` row (once for `a`, once for `b`) and keeps the product and the `x^K` scaling in
  registers. Single-thread, one `(b_med, chunk)` call: 178 ns -> 47 ns.
* `simd.rs::bit_transpose_8x64_avx2` keeps the 8x8 byte transpose in two `__m256i`, so the
  three mask/shift rounds run four 64-bit lanes at a time. It serves both
  `zerocheck::univariate_skip_optimized`'s 64-byte transpose and the lincheck bank fold
  (`lincheck/union.rs::bank_transpose`), which previously fell back to two SSE2 calls per
  eight-row run. Single-thread: 13.9 ns -> 4.4 ns per 64-byte transpose (the AVX-512 VBMI
  body measures 2.7 ns).

Both bodies are selected through the same runtime feature checks, are byte-identical to the
portable kernels, and keep the SSE2 and portable bodies for CPUs below the AVX2 tier.

## 10. Prover-only: serial Frobenius table build

`src/pcs/block_stats_portable.rs::frob_tables` builds its 8 MiB table inside a
`OnceLock::get_or_init`. The build is serial: with `into_par_iter`, several
workers entering the initializer at once occupy the Rayon pool that the
initializer's parallel build needs, and the process deadlocks. The tables are
built once, so the serial build costs a few milliseconds per process.
